    <script src="https://hyperliquid.statuspage.io/embed/script.js"></script><iframe src="https://h20qtjygwppc.statuspage.io/embed/frame" title="Hyperliquid Status" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" style="position: fixed; border-width: medium; border-style: none; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: none; box-shadow: rgba(9, 20, 66, 0.25) 0px 20px 32px -8px; z-index: 9999; transition: left 1s, bottom 1s, right 1s; height: 115px; width: 320px; left: -9999px; right: -9999px; bottom: 60px;"></iframe>
    <!--
      Minimal `process` global for the browserify shims that vite.config.ts
      aliases node builtins to. `readable-stream` (reached via
      stream-browserify, in turn via crypto-browserify) reads `process.browser`
      and `process.version` at MODULE SCOPE:

        var i = !process.browser && ['v0.10','v0.9.'].indexOf(
          process.version.slice(0, 5)) > -1 ? setImmediate : nextTick

      so it throws "process is not defined" during import, before React mounts.
      webpack provided a process shim for CRA; vite does not.

      `define` cannot cover this: it rewrites `process.env` textually but leaves
      bare `process` alone. This has to be a real global, and it has to exist
      before any module evaluates -- hence a classic script here rather than an
      import, since those are deferred.

      Deliberately tiny: only what the shims actually touch. `env` is present
      for safety but unused, because `define` replaces `process.env` at build
      time.
    -->
    <script>
      window.process = window.process || {
        env: {},
        browser: true,
        version: "",
        versions: {},
        platform: "browser",
        nextTick: function (callback) {
          queueMicrotask(callback);
        },
      };
    </script>
